6587.subject: Biology
6587.question_text: An association between the root nodule of a leguminous plant and rhizobium sp, is known as
6587.explanation:
The association between the root nodule of a leguminous plant and rhizobium sp is a symbiotic relationship that benefits both the plant and the bacteria.

Rhizobium bacteria are soil bacteria that infect the roots of leguminous plants and cause the formation of nitrogen-fixing nodules. The bacteria convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia, which the plant can use for growth and development.  Leguminous plants on the other hand with their plant roots provide food to the rhizobia in the form of carbohydrates, such as malate and succinate.

Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic relationship between the roots of plants and fungi that benefits both organisms.

6588.subject: Biology
6588.explanation:
Amphibians are mostly semi-aquatic and spend part of their time on land and part in water. They typically start out as larvae living in water, but some species have developed behavioural adaptations to bypass this.  

Amphibians require moist habitats, and relative humidities of about 80% work well for most species. Hence, they live in water as well as a moist land. Option B

options.text: in water and on moist land

6589.subject: Biology
6589.explanation: Among animals, viviparity is development of the embryo inside the body of the parent, eventually leading to live birth, as opposed to reproduction by laying eggs that complete their incubation outside the parental body. This is found mainly in mammals.

6590.subject: Biology
6590.question_text: The jointed structure in insects that bears organs which are sensitive to touch, smell and vibration is the
6590.explanation:
The Antennae are sensory organs that are made up of one or more jointed segments and are attached to the first one or two segments of the insect's head. 

Insects have paired antennae so they can smell in stereo. The jointed structure in insects that bears organs sensitive to touch, smell, and vibration is the antennae

6591.subject: Biology
6591.question_text: Which of following groups is the most advanced?
6591.explanation:
Pteridophytes don't have seeds. They propagate by spores. · Gymnosperms are the earliest seed plants. Gymnosperms have advanced reproductive structures compared to pteridophytes. Gymnosperms produce seeds as well. Gymnosperms are the most advanced. Option D is the correct answer

Thallophyta- body not differentiated into roots and stem,no vascular system,no seed formation

Bryophyta- body differentiated but lack vascular system,no seed formation

Pteridophyta- well- differentiated body, vascular system present, no seeds formation

Gymnosperms- well-differentiated body with vascular system, seeds are naked(not enclosed in a fruit)

Angiosperms- well-differentiated body with vascular system, seeds are covered(enclosed in a fruit)

6592.subject: Biology
6592.question_text: Most monocots are easily recognized by their
6592.explanation: Many monocot leaves are sword-shaped. Monocot leaves are typically narrow and elongated, with parallel veins that run from the base of the leaf to its tip.

6593.subject: Biology
6593.question_text: Water fleas, wood lice and barnacles belong to the group?
6593.explanation: Crabs, prawns, lobsters, barnacles, wood lice and water fleas belong to the class Crustaceans as aquatic free living animals

6594.subject: Biology
6594.question_text: The mode of feeding in Amoeba and Hydra is
6594.explanation:
Amoeba and hydra are both heterotrophs, meaning they consume organic material and smaller organisms.

Holophytic nutrition is the same as autotrophic nutrition. Both terms refer to the process by which organisms create their own food using inorganic materials, such as water, carbon dioxide, and mineral salts, in the presence of sunlight. 

Symbiotic nutrition is a type of interaction between two organisms where they share shelter and nourishment, and both benefit from the relationship.

6595.subject: Biology
6595.question_text: Which of the following organisms does not exist as a single free living cell?
6595.explanation: Mold is a multicellular fungus.Mold is a living organism that grows in a network of hyphae called a mycelium. The mycelium is the visible part of mold. Mold reproduces by releasing spores into the air, which can then settle in a new area.

6596.subject: Biology
6596.question_text: The center for learning and memory in the human brain is the
6596.explanation:
Medulla oblongata is the bottom-most part of your brain. Its location means it's where your brain and spinal cord connect, making it a key conduit for nerve signals to and from your body. It also helps control vital processes like your heartbeat, breathing and blood pressure.

The cerebellum coordinates and regulates muscle tone, balance, and posture. The cerebellum plays a role in higher-order functions, including cognitive, emotional, and reward processes.

The Cerebrum is the largest part of the brain, making up about 80% of it. It's responsible for memory, intelligence, emotions, personality, and more. It is the center for intelligence, memory, and emotions. It coordinates voluntary muscle movements and helps in maintaining posture and balance.

The olfactory lobe's main function is to transmit the sense of smell.

6597.subject: Biology
6597.explanation:
The functions of the heart are to pump blood and oxygen around the body and deliver waste products (carbon dioxide) back to the lungs to be removed. 

Urea is produced in the liver:  

  • Production: The liver produces urea through a series of biochemical reactions called the urea cycle. The urea cycle converts ammonia, a toxic waste product from the breakdown of amino acids, into urea, which is nontoxic and water-soluble.  
  • Transport: Urea is dissolved into the blood and transported to the kidneys.  
  • Excretion: The kidneys excrete urea in urine along with water and other waste products.

6598.subject: Biology
6598.question_text: The structure that holds the yolk in position is labelled
6598.explanation:
I - Albumin

II - Shell

III - Chalaza

IV - Germinal disc

The chalazae are a pair of spring-like structures that project from the equatorial region of the vitelline membrane into the albumen and are considered to act as balancers, maintaining the yolk in a steady position in the laid egg.

6600.question_text: The gas produced during tissue respiration can be identified by using
6600.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO\(_2\) is the gas produced during tissue respiration. And it can be identified by bringing it close to lime water ( Calcium hydroxide), which turns the lime water solution milky.

6601.subject: Biology
6601.question_text: A seedling grown in the dark is likely to be
6601.explanation: A seedling grown in the dark will eventually die because it won't have enough energy or food to grow. Seedlings grown in the dark grow taller than seedlings grown in the light, but without much leaf development. This is because they use stored chemical energy in their cells to grow. They become etiolated(pale and drawn out due to a lack of light).

6602.subject: Biology
6602.question_text: The enzyme invertase will hydrolyze sucrose to give
6602.explanation: Sucrose is a dissacharide that resulted from reaction of 1 molecule of Glucose and 1molecule of fructose.However, Sucrose can be split into Glucose and fructose in the presence of an enzyme, invertase.

6603.subject: Biology
6603.question_text: When yeast respire anaerobically, it converts simple sugar to carbon (IV) oxide and
6603.explanation:
When yeast breaks down sugar through anaerobic respiration, it produces ethanol, carbon dioxide, and energy. This process is also known as fermentation.

Yeast uses anaerobic respiration when oxygen is not available. This type of respiration is important economically because it's used to make foods like bread and alcoholic drinks.

6604.subject: Biology
6604.question_text: The transportation of oxygen and carbon (IV) oxide in mammals is carried out by
6604.explanation:
White blood cells are also called leukocytes. They protect you against illness and disease. Think of white blood cells as your immunity cells.

Platelets, or thrombocytes, are small, colourless cell fragments in our blood that form clots and stop or prevent bleeding. Platelets are made in our bone marrow, the sponge-like tissue inside our bones.

Phagocytes are a type of white blood cell (leukocyte) that are part of the immune system's defense mechanism. 

Red blood cells (RBCs) transport oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues. RBCs contain hemoglobin, a protein that binds to oxygen. The Red blood cells are also referred to as erythrocytes.

6605.subject: Biology
6605.question_text: The veins of the leaf are formed by the
6605.explanation: The veins of a leaf are formed by the vascular tissue within the leaf, which branches out from the midrib to form a network structure.

6606.subject: Biology
6606.question_text: The parts which function together to bring about hearing are labelled
6606.explanation:
The parts of the ear that enable hearing are the outer ear, middle ear, and inner ear, and the auditory nerve:  

  • Outer ear: Sound waves enter the ear through the ear canal and hit the eardrum.  
  • Middle ear: The eardrum vibrates and sends vibrations to the malleus, incus, and stapes, three tiny bones that amplify the sound vibrations.  
  • Inner ear: The vibrations are sent to the cochlea, a snail-shaped organ that contains fluid and hair cells. The vibrations cause the fluid to ripple, which moves the hair cells. The hair cells bend, which opens pore-like channels that send an electrical signal to the brain via the auditory nerve. The brain interprets the electrical signal as sound.  
  • Auditory nerve: Carries the electrical signal from the inner ear to the brain.

6616.question_text: Blood vessel usually pass through the structure labelled
6616.explanation: The transverse foramina are small holes in the vertebrae that allow the vertebral arteries, veins, and sympathetic nerves to pass through. The vertebral arteries supply blood to the brainstem and cerebellum by entering the foramen magnum. (labelled V in the diagram). Option C

6617.subject: Biology
6617.question_text: Salts and water are absorbed in the roots and transported to leaves by
6617.explanation: The water and salts are absorbed by the root hair and undergo cell to cell movement by osmosis until they reach the xylem. This water is then transported through the xylem vessels to the leaves and is evaporated by the process of transpiration.

6620.subject: Biology
6620.question_text: The number of plants species obtained from a population study of a garden is as follows: Guinea grass (15), Ipomea spp (5), sida spp (7) and Imperata spp (23). What is the percentage of occurrence of Imperata spp?
6620.explanation:
Total number of species = 15 + 5 + 7 + 23 = 50

Total number of Imperata spp = 23

Percentage occurence of Imperata spp = number of imperata/ total number of species X 100

                                                                = \(\frac{23}{50}\)\(\times 100\)

                                                                = 46% - Option C

6623.subject: Biology
6623.question_text: Carbon (IV) oxide content of the atmosphere is least affected by
6623.explanation:
Apart from cutting down and clearing of forests, in the other options,Carbon (IV) oxide content of the atmosphere is greatly affected.

When forests are cut down or burned, the stored carbon is released into the atmosphere as CO\(_2\).

options.text: cutting down and clearing of forests

6624.subject: Biology
6624.question_text: The factor that least affects food shortages in sub-saharan Africa is
6624.explanation:
Food production in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is affected by a number of factors, including climate change, the need for increased investment, and the need for structural change to the farming system. Mixed-cropping least affects food shortages because Mixed cropping, or mixed crop-livestock farming, is a dominant agricultural model in sub-Saharan Africa. some of the reasons are due to:

Environmental and social concerns: Mixed farming is promoted to address environmental and social concerns.  

Food security: Mixed crop-livestock systems are important for the food security of poor people in developing countries.  

Risk minimization: Farmers use mixed cropping to minimize losses due to rainfall variability and pest. 

Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) experiences heavy flooding, and the frequency and intensity of these events is increasing.

6625.subject: Biology
6625.question_text: The epiphytic habitat can best be described as
6625.explanation:
The epiphytic habitat is a moist, tropical environment where epiphytic plants grow on other plants for support, and access nutrients and sunlight:  

Epiphytes are found in tropical and temperate regions, and are often found in dense, shaded forests- where we have many trees (Arboreal)

6627.subject: Biology
6627.question_text: The highest percentage of energy in an ecosystem occurs at the level of the
6627.explanation: Producers have the highest percentage of energy in an ecosystem. Producers, such as plants, are at the base of the food chain and have the most energy. They use energy from the sun to create organic sugar.

6628.subject: Biology
6628.question_text: The greatest influence on a stable ecosystem in nature is exerted by
6628.explanation: Humans, animals, and rainfall all have an impact on the stability of an ecosystem, but humans have the greatest influence. Humans have a pervasive influence on all ecosystems on Earth, and many are directly dominated by humans. Some of the influence are negative and they include pollution, deforestation, burning fossil fuels, Agriculture, habitat loss, over-harvesting etc

6630.subject: Biology
6630.question_text: The physical space occupied by an organism together with its functional role in community can be described as
6630.explanation: An organism's niche is the role it plays in an ecosystem, including the conditions it needs to survive and reproduce, and its interactions with other organisms.

6639.explanation: A hygrometer is a device that measures the humidity, or amount of water vapor, in the air

6640.question_text: The distribution of plants in a rain forest is governed mainly by
6640.explanation: Several factors govern the distribution of plants in a rainforest, including temperature and rainfall

6642.question_text: Both recessive and dominant characters are found
6642.explanation: Both recessive and dominant characters can be found at the same locus of a homologous chromosome. Chromosomes in a homologous pair have the same genes in the same order, but they may have different alleles. Option B is the correct answer

6644.subject: Biology
6644.question_text: The probability of a baby being a boy or a girl depends on the contribution of the
6644.explanation: The probability of a baby being a boy or a girl depends on the father's sex cells because sperm cells can have either an X or a Y chromosome, while eggs always have an X chromosome.

6648.subject: Biology
6648.question_text: Which of the following is likely to encourage inbreeding in plants?
6648.explanation: Hermaphrodite (or bisexual) flowers contain both male (stamens) and female (carpels) reproductive organs within the same flower. Because these organs are physically close and often mature simultaneously, there is a high likelihood of self-pollination, which directly leads to inbreeding.

6650.subject: Biology
6650.question_text: A tall plants crossed with a dwarf one produces offspring of which half are tall and half are dwarf. What are the genotypes of the parents?
6650.explanation:
The parents' genotypes are:

Heterozygous Tall ( Tt ) and Homozygous for  Dwarfism ( tt )

6651.subject: Biology
6651.question_text: In man, the ability to roll the tongue is a variation classified as
6651.explanation:
Physiological variation is when members of the same species react to their environment differently. Here are some examples of physiological variation in humans and animals. E.g People have different abilities to taste phenylthiocarbamide (PTC), roll their tongues, and have different blood types.

Morphological variation is the difference in the structure and form of organisms, which can occur within or between species. It can be caused by genetic factors, environmental factors, or a combination of both. Some examples of morphological variation include: Hair colour, hair quantity, extra body parts, and missing body parts in humans.

6653.subject: Biology
6653.question_text: Darwin is considered the first scientist who correctly explained the theory of
6653.explanation:
Special creation - Louis Pasteur

Spontaneous generation - Aristotle 

Use and disuse - Jean Baptiste Lamarck

Charles Darwin is known as the first scientist to propose the theory of evolution by natural selection.

6655.subject: Biology
6655.question_text: The stem of a typical aquatic plant usually has many
6655.explanation: Aquatic plants have large air cavities in their stems, leaves, and roots, which are called aerenchyma. Aerenchyma is a spongy tissue that creates air channels and gaps in the plant. These air cavities help the plant float and provide buoyancy.

6656.subject: Biology
6656.question_text: The role of the male adult honey bee is to
6656.explanation: The main role of a male honey bee, also known as a drone, is to mate with the queen bee in order to fertilize new queens.

6657.subject: Biology
6657.question_text: The ability of an organism to live successfully in an environment is known as
6657.explanation: Adaptation is a heritable trait that helps an organism survive and reproduce in its environment. Adaptations can be behavioral, morphological, or physiological. They can be the result of a gene mutation that improves an organism's ability to survive and reproduce. Over time, the mutation becomes more common as it passes to offspring.

6659.subject: Biology
6659.question_text: The most important adaptation of xerophytes is the ability of the protoplasm to
6659.explanation: Xerophytes are plants that have adapted to survive in dry environments, such as deserts, salt marshes, and saline soils. The most adaptation is to resist being damaged by loss of water

options.text: resist being damaged by loss of water
store sugar and minerals in the vacuoles

6661.subject: Biology
6661.question_text: A green snake in green grass is able to escape notice from predators because of its
6661.explanation:
Disruptive coloration is a camouflage technique that uses contrasting patterns to break up an animal's outline and make it harder to see.

Countershading is a type of camouflage where an animal's upper body is darker than its underside.

Warning coloration is a defense mechanism used by animals to warn predators that they are toxic, distasteful, or have other harmful qualities.

Cryptic colouration, also known as camouflage, is a defense mechanism that helps organisms hide their identity, location, and movement by blending in with their surroundings. It's a common form of visual camouflage that uses color patterns to make it harder for predators to see the organism.

6663.subject: Biology
6663.question_text: For heterotrophic organisms, competition is least caused by the inadequacy of
6663.explanation: Among autotrophs, Light is the major cause of competition because they need sunlight to manufacture their food and survive unlike heterotrophs. Hence,competition is least caused by inadequacy of light.
